state.title: Invoice count on the invoices page

task.text: Show the number of invoices above the invoices table on the invoices page, with a unit or browser test.

summaries.summary:
The invoices page now shows how many invoices there are, in a line directly above the table. With today's single sample invoice it reads "1 invoice". The count comes from the list of invoices the page actually renders, so it stays correct when more are added, and it says "invoices" for any number other than one ("0 invoices", "3 invoices").

How to try it: run `TZ=UTC SANDBOX_DATA_DIR=.sandbox-data npm start` and open http://127.0.0.1:4173/invoices. "1 invoice" appears between the "Invoices" heading and the table.

What changed:
- src/invoices/index.ts: new `invoiceCountLabel(count)` helper that handles singular and plural.
- src/web/server.ts: the invoices page now builds its table rows from a small `invoices` list (still the same single "Invoice 1" at 25.00) and puts the count label above the table. Invoice names are now escaped the same way the customers page already escapes its values.
- Tests: a unit test for the label (0, 1 and 3) in src/invoices/index.test.ts, and the invoices browser spec now also checks that "1 invoice" is visible.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry, because the CI changelog check fails without one.

There was no plan.md, so I followed the existing code's style.

Tests run: the invoices unit tests (3 passed), the type check (`npm run lint`, clean) and the invoices browser spec (1 passed). Playwright's own browsers are not installed on this machine, so I ran the browser spec against the system Chrome using a temporary config, which I deleted afterwards. Nothing about that is committed.

Every check passed. The invoices page shows "1 invoice" on its own line, between the "Invoices" heading and the table, at both desktop and phone widths. Nothing else on the site changed.

**What I checked**
- **Project test command** (`TZ=UTC SANDBOX_DATA_DIR=.sandbox-data npm test`, run once in full): 2 test files, 4 tests, all passed. That includes the new invoice count label test (0, 1 and 3). Output is in .jv-evidence/tests.txt.
- **Browser walk-through**: I started the app on a free port (4391) and clicked through it in Chrome at 1440×900 and 390×844. All 22 checks passed (11 per width):
  - /invoices loads, shows "1 invoice" directly under the heading and right before the table, and the table still has one row: Invoice 1 at 25.00.
  - No sideways scrolling on the invoices page at either width.
  - The site root (/) shows the same invoices page with the count.
  - The "Customers" nav link opens the Customers page, which has no invoice count. The "Invoices" link goes back and the count is still there.
  
  Results are in .jv-evidence/journeys.txt.
- **The project's own browser tests** (tests/browser: invoices and customers): 2 of 2 passed. Playwright's bundled browsers aren't installed here, so I pointed a throwaway config (.jv-evidence/pw.config.ts) at the system Chrome and the server I started. Output is in .jv-evidence/browser-spec.txt.

**What I couldn't check**
- With today's single hard-coded invoice, the page can only show "1 invoice". "0 invoices" and "3 invoices" are covered by the unit test only, not in the browser.
- The Customers table is empty because there is no customer data in .sandbox-data. That was already the case before this change, and the change doesn't touch that page.

I stopped the dev server I started. I changed no code and committed nothing; everything I added is in .jv-evidence/, which git ignores.

checks.summary: Invoices unit tests: 3/3 passed, including the new count-label test. Type check clean. Invoices browser spec: 1/1 passed, including the new '1 invoice' check.

checks.summary: Unit tests: 4/4 passed in 2 files. Browser journeys: 22/22 checks passed at desktop and phone widths. Project browser tests: 2/2 passed. No failures.

Documentation-only and test-only changes outside the risky areas whose checks passed land.

state.title: Unit test for an untested pure function in src

task.text:
What: pick one pure function in src/ (no I/O, no server, no shared state) that no existing unit test covers, and add a vitest unit test for it covering the normal case and at least one edge case (empty input, zero, rounding, or whatever fits the function).
Why: the owner wants better unit coverage of the pure logic. Earlier today three investigations (TTERC0P, TYDEGY7, TGWQM7P, "Pure functions in src/ without a unit test") looked for such functions; their reports may name candidates.
Where: src/invoices/index.ts and src/customers/index.ts are the likely places; tests live next to the source as *.test.ts (for example src/invoices/index.test.ts). Do not change the function's behaviour; if the test reveals a bug, stop and report it as a decision instead of fixing it.
Done when: the new test passes with `npm test`, `npm run lint` is clean, the pull request says which function was chosen and why it counted as untested, and any changelog requirement of the repository is met. Publish a pull request.

summaries.summary:
The HTML escape helper used on the customers page now has its own unit test.

**Which function and why it counted as untested:** I checked every pure function in src/. All three in src/invoices/index.ts (`lineTotalCents`, `invoiceTotalCents`, `invoiceDate`) are already called by src/invoices/index.test.ts. src/customers/index.ts has no pure functions: everything there reads or writes files. That left `escape` in src/web/server.ts. It turns customer names and VAT numbers into safe HTML. No test touches it, and none could, because importing server.ts opens the customer store and starts the web server.

**What changed:**
- I moved `escape` exactly as it was into a new file, src/web/html.ts, and server.ts now imports it from there. The page output is the same.
- New src/web/html.test.ts with 4 tests: plain text stays the same (normal case); `&`, `<` and `"` are escaped together; an existing entity like `<` has its `&` escaped once; empty text stays empty (edge cases).
- CHANGELOG.md has an entry, which the CI `check:changelog` step requires.

**How to try it:** `TZ=UTC SANDBOX_DATA_DIR=.sandbox-data npx vitest run src/web/html.test.ts`, or the full `npm test`.

**No plan.md** was in the worktree, so I followed the task text. One departure: the task pointed at src/invoices and src/customers, but neither has an untested pure function, so the chosen function is in src/web.

**Possible bug found while looking (not fixed, outside this test):** `lineTotalCents` uses `Math.floor(unitPrice * 100)`, and floating-point error makes it lose a cent on some prices. A unit price of 0.29 gives 28 cents, 1.13 gives 112 and 19.99 gives 1998. The current tests only use whole-number prices, so they don't catch it. I left the function and its tests alone, as the task said, but it may be worth its own task.

Everything passed. The new unit test for the HTML escape helper runs and passes, and the Customers and Invoices pages behave the same after `escape` moved to src/web/html.ts. **What I checked** - **Branch changes compared with main:** CHANGELOG.md, the new src/web/html.ts (`escape` copied over unchanged), the new src/web/html.test.ts, and src/web/server.ts (now imports `escape` instead of defining it). - **Test command** `TZ=UTC SANDBOX_DATA_DIR=.sandbox-data npm test`, run once: 3 files, 7 of 7 tests passed. All 4 new `escape` tests passed (plain text, & < " together, existing entity escaped once, empty text). The existing customer and invoice tests also passed. Output is in .jv-evidence/tests.txt. - **Other checks:** `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) passed with no errors. `npm run check:changelog` passed. - **Browser journeys** (Playwright with Chromium, run against `npm start`'s server.ts on ports 4391/4392 using test data under .jv-evidence/), at 1440×900 and 390×844: - **Invoices page:** the heading appears and the total shows 25.00. From there I clicked the Customers link. - **Customers page with four seeded customers:** names and VAT numbers containing `&`, `<`, `"` and HTML tags (`Smith & Sons <"Ltd">`, `GB99`) appear as plain text. No `` element gets into the page and no dialog opens. Text that already holds entities (`Already <escaped> Co`, `ES&1`) also appears exactly as typed. A very long name wraps, and all 4 rows show. `/api/customers` responds. - **Customers page with no customers:** the heading and column headers show over an empty table. - All 32 checks passed. **Small thing I noticed (not caused by this change):** at phone width, a very long VAT number with no spaces pushes the page about 20px wider than the screen, so it scrolls sideways a little (see customers-seeded-phone.png). The page layout was already like that and this branch doesn't touch it. **Housekeeping:** I changed no code and committed nothing. I stopped both servers I started. Everything I added is under .jv-evidence/: the screenshots, tests.txt, the throwaway script journey.mjs and the test data folders.

checks.summary: The 4 new escape tests in src/web/html.test.ts passed; tsc --noEmit was clean. Per step instructions only the new test file was run, not the full suite.

checks.summary: npm test: 3 files, 7/7 tests passed (including the 4 new escape tests). Lint and changelog check passed. Browser journeys: 32/32 checks passed across invoices, customers seeded and customers empty, at desktop and phone widths. Nothing failed.

task.text:

Production behaviour, in the routes, means deployed systems, live data, credentials, billing, infrastructure and deploy configuration, not the ordinary feature, UI, test or documentation changes every task makes. A small change outside the risky areas that the passing checks cover lands; a behaviour change the checks do not exercise is verify-then-land. When two routes fit about equally, choose the more cautious one.

criteria.land: Small or low-risk change outside the project's risky areas, covered by the checks that passed.
criteria.verify-then-land: A behaviour change the checks do not exercise, or a medium-sized change, outside the risky areas.
criteria.ask-owner: Touches a risky area, changes stored data or production behaviour, or is large or hard to undo.
